title: SDOH Screening in Clinical Settings: Tools, Z-Codes & Referrals
summary: How clinical teams screen for social needs using validated tools (PRAPARE, AHC, SEEK), document with ICD-10 Z-codes, and connect patients to community resources.

objectives.text: Identify validated SDOH screening tools and their appropriate use cases
Explain how Z-codes are used to document social needs in clinical records
Describe the closed-loop referral model for connecting patients to community resources

content_blocks.body:
SDOH screening asks patients about their social needs directly — food security, housing stability, transportation, utilities, interpersonal safety. The evidence shows patients are willing to answer these questions when asked in a respectful, confidential context, and that screening identifies needs that clinicians would not otherwise know about.

But screening without action causes harm: asking someone if they're food insecure and then having no response to offer erodes trust. Effective SDOH programs pair screening with a referral pathway — either through embedded community health workers, a care coordination team, or a community resource platform like findhelp or NowPow.
content_blocks.heading: Screening: from asking to acting

items.body: Protocol for Responding to and Assessing Patients' Assets, Risks, and Experiences. 21-item tool from NACHC. Maps to Z-codes. Most widely used in FQHCs.
items.title: PRAPARE

items.body: Accountable Health Communities screening tool developed by CMS. 10 core questions covering food, housing, transportation, utilities, and safety. Required for CMS AHC model participants.
items.title: AHC Screening Tool

items.body: Safe Environment for Every Kid. Pediatric tool designed for primary care. Screens for family stress, substance use, depression, and food insecurity during well-child visits.
items.title: SEEK

items.body: Brief 5-question tool for rapid screening in high-volume settings. Covers food, housing, transportation, interpersonal violence, and utilities.
items.title: SDOH-5

content_blocks.body:
ICD-10-CM Z-codes (in the Z55–Z65 range) capture social determinants of health in clinical documentation:

- Z59.0: Homelessness
- Z59.4: Lack of adequate food
- Z63.0: Problems in relationship with spouse or partner
- Z56.0: Unemployment, unspecified
- Z60.2: Problems related to living alone

Z-codes enable population-level analysis of social needs in a practice or system, support quality reporting, and increasingly are used by payers to adjust risk scores and target interventions. Documentation of Z-codes has historically been low — many clinicians don't know they exist or don't realize the clinical and operational value of using them.
content_blocks.heading: Z-codes: documenting social needs in ICD-10

content_blocks.body: A warm referral to a food bank is better than a pamphlet. A closed-loop referral — where the receiving organization confirms the patient connected with services and sends that information back to the care team — is better still. Community resource platforms like findhelp (formerly Aunt Bertha), NowPow, and Unite Us are building the infrastructure for closed-loop referrals at scale.
content_blocks.heading: Closed-loop referrals: did the patient get help?
